text: In the Shannon-Hartley theorem, what does doubling the transmit power (+3 dB) buy at high SNR?
choices: One additional bit per symbol per hertz
explanation: Capacity is logarithmic in SNR, so at high SNR each doubling of power adds log2(2) = 1 bit/symbol/Hz. Going from 30 to 33 dB takes you from about 10 to about 11 bits/Hz — a 10% gain for double the power. Capacity is linear in bandwidth, which is why the industry chases spectrum rather than watts.
